items.title: Here’s Why Scout Isn’t Doing Removable Doors and Roofs Yet
items.summary:
Scout might be staking its claim as the electric truck brand for serious off-roaders and explorers who need ladder-frame power and dependability, but it’s not necessarily angling to replace the Wrangler and Bronco on their turf.

During his appearance on The Drivecast , Scout CEO Scott Keogh said that removable doors and roof panels are not something the revived brand is planning—at least, not yet.

“We’ve been interacting with the Scout community—actually, we showed the first concept to the Scout OGs before we showed the journalists,” Keogh said. “We invited them down to Dallas, and look—the number one thing we wanted to do was build an authentic, credible, rugged vehicle. Hence body-on-frame, hence solid rear axle, hence mechanical switches and door handles, all those kind of things. So, 100% we’ve achieved that. We will not do removable doors and removable tops on the Traveler as we know it.”

Scout Motors 

Keogh said if Scout props up another model, a three-row SUV would be a likely candidate. Given that, the potential for a more modular SUV with optional panels, in the vein of the Wrangler and Bronco, seems like a far-off consideration. But he didn’t shut the door.

“Is there some future we would look at that type of vehicle? 100%,” Keogh added. “For the Traveler and for this Terra, no. Why did we make that decision? If you look at the application and the market and everything we wanted to achieve, this is the best way achieving it—the vehicle that you’re seeing right here, without a doubt.”

Considering what it’s taken Scout to get to this point, and the…
items.t: Here’s Why Scout Isn’t Doing Removable Doors and Roofs Yet

items.title: 2026 Lexus TX350 Pros and Cons Review: A Great SUV Disgraced by Awful Tech
items.summary:
Once upon a time, a car was just a car. Nowadays it’s like: does it have Apple CarPlay ? Is it a “normal” engine or a hybrid, plug-in hybrid, or EV? Do I have to pay for a heated seats subscription, and will the car give away my private info to every company in the world? Man, I miss simpler times, which is why I can’t recommend the 2026 Lexus TX350 , even though it’s a pretty great SUV.

The TX350 is the fancier, dressed-up version of the pretty-great Toyota Grand Highlander . It seats six (seven if you go for the middle bench), has a spacious cabin, a superbly comfortable ride (like, really comfortable), and, frankly, I think it looks alright. By most standards, anyone looking for a great family luxury SUV could do a lot worse than this. Plus, it’s a Lexus, so the resale value will hold up for years. But then you get into the usability, and that’s when things go down the toilet.

Lexus 

Cons 

I could spell things out, or I could show you what I hated about the TX350. Just watch the video below. 

I also disliked the infotainment system and the screen itself. It’s not intuitive, and the screen is big just for the sake of being big. The OS doesn’t take full advantage of the screen’s size, and you usually just end up with humongous CarPlay or a huge map, rather than sectioned-off bits of the screen to display multiple pieces of information. Plus, I can’t deal with a car that requires tapping on a screen to increase or decrease the fan speed. Some things should just always be physical buttons.

items.title: Scout CEO Says Rivian Isn’t a Direct Competitor. He’s Wrong
items.summary:
Until we start seeing new Scouts on the road, we’re left analyzing stats and specs to see what kind of vehicles these will be. Obviously, they’re electrified 4x4s, but are they more like Broncos with batteries or Rivians with an available gas range extender? If you ask Scout Motors CEO Scott Keogh, the answer is “neither, really.”

While we know a large percentage of Scout reservation holders are currently Bronco owners , that doesn’t exactly mean the two off-roaders are analogous. In my mind, the Rivian comparison has been top of mind because they’re both billed as new electric adventure brands. (I’m not sure if you can call Rivian a startup anymore.) But Keogh insists that Scout exists in a different lane.

“Look, I think anyone selling a truck and SUV and doing something cool is a competitor. So let’s not be naive,” Keogh explained on The Drivecast , our website’s weekly show. “I think you’re crazy to so finely slice the market. Do I see them [Rivian] as a direct competitor, massive cross-shop? No.”

Rivian 

Keogh continued, “Who do I see as the competitors? If I look at the Traveler world, I would see vehicles like the Toyota Land Cruiser. [I’d] see vehicles, obviously, like the Bronco. Even to go a little bit higher-end, the Defender is the definite cross-shop. If I look on the other side, definitely Ford, definitely Chevy, and a little bit of Rivian in there. But the difference between, let’s say, our truck—it’s a whole different philosophy.”

The Scout head honcho went on to explain why. For starters, the Traveler SUV and Terra will be full-size, rather than…
items.t: Scout CEO Says Rivian Isn’t a Direct Competitor. He’s Wrong

items.title: The 2027 Hyundai Elantra Has the Wildest Fenders I’ve Ever Seen on a Basic Sedan
items.summary:
Hyundai ’s design is the most fluid in the business, and the wave that hit the Tucson a few weeks back is now crashing on the brand’s compact sedan. The 2027 Elantra marks the four-door’s eighth generation, and certainly its boldest fashion statement yet.

An “everyday muscle car” is how the company defined it in a presentation to media, and while its performance figures might not exactly support that claim, the bulging fenders, three-box silhouette, and retro-forward lines allow you to follow the logic.

The new Elantra is wider than ever before at 73 inches, and 3.4 inches longer than the outgoing car, with 1.2 inches of that between the wheels. That length was added for second-row passengers, as Hyundai tells it, who will also benefit from an extra 0.7 inches of headroom.

Adam Ismail 

Dimensionally, the Elantra is ticking closer to the midsize Sonata, yet Hyundai promises a curb weight below 3,000 pounds. The new Elantra will land in the U.S. first in gas-only guise, with a 147-horsepower, 138 lb-ft SmartStream 2.0 four-cylinder targeting 35 mpg. A conventional hybrid will come slightly later, as a 2028 model, and it’s clearly positioned more for fuel economy than additional power, as it only packs 8 extra hp but is estimated to average 53 mpg.

One small but important note: a multi-link independent rear suspension is exclusive to the hybrid. The regular Elantra makes do with a torsion beam.

Adam Ismail 

Arguably more controversial than the Elantra’s exterior is its interior, with a massive 12.9-inch center infotainment screen as standard, supplemented by a slim…
items.t: The 2027 Hyundai Elantra Has the Wildest Fenders I’ve Ever Seen on a Basic Sedan

items.title: A Speed-Limit Glitch Sparked a Messy Fight Over the 2026 Baja 1000 Win: Explained
items.summary:
Ensenada-born Trophy Truck champ Alan Ampudia was first to cross the 2026 Baja 1000 finish line, declared the unofficial winner , and allowed to celebrate on stage. A day later, he was told he’d come in second. Post-race corrections are not uncommon in desert racing, but this one put race organizers in a particularly sticky situation.

Ampudia and Australian co-driver Paul Weel brought Team Papas’ No. 1 Trophy Truck into San José del Cabo early on Saturday, November 14, 13.5 seconds ahead of Bryce Menzies and Andy McMillin in the No. 7 on raw time. When SCORE International posted corrected results on Sunday, Menzies and McMillin had won by 1 minute, 38 seconds.

The swing came from a timing adjustment to one speed-zone section north of Loreto. Ampudia says it cost him a win he earned by following the rules. Fans are divided on the strength of his case, and even the winners aren’t fully celebrating.

Alan Ampudia 

Paul Weel 

Bryce Menzies 

Andy McMillin 
 SCORE, Jack Wright Media 

This year’s race was the first run entirely in Baja California Sur, a roughly 950-mile loop from Cabo to Cabo. I was in the mix myself, co-driving a TrophyLite running in Class 2, way, way behind the Trophy Trucks—look for that feature story soon. Meanwhile, here’s the drama from the front of the pack.

What Happened 

Speed zones are routine in Baja. Where the course runs on or across public highways, racers are held to a posted limit, and SCORE’s Stella satellite tracker logs penalties for going over. Time in a speed zone normally still counts toward a team’s total; otherwise, it would be a…
items.t: A Speed-Limit Glitch Sparked a Messy Fight Over the 2026 Baja 1000 Win: Explained

items.title: Genesis’ First Hybrids Use a Four-Cylinder. The Torque Matches the Twin-Turbo V6
items.summary:
Genesis has moved as quickly as it could to shift course from its electric future and tip toe into electrification with a hybrid strategy. Two years after announcing the shift the automaker’s ready to show off its first hybrids.

On Thursday, at the 2026 Los Angeles auto show Genesis debuted the GV80 hybrid crossover SUV and G80 hybrid luxury sedan. Both feature a turbocharged hybrid powertrain, both feature turbo-six-like torque, and both tout significant efficiency gains.

Under the hood of both models sits a hybrid 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four powertrain mounted longitudinally due to the models’ rear-wheel-drive architectures. Total system output is rated at 347 horsepower and 391 lb-ft of torque, the latter of which is comparable to the current twin-turbo V6 powertrain available in both models today. A seven-speed automatic transmission will handle shifting duties and regenerative braking is onboard and adjustable.

Genesis said the GV80 Hybrid’s powertrain nets a fuel economy improvement of 24% while that jumps to 30% in the G80 Hybrid to the respective gas-only models. It’s unclear if that’s for the city, highway, combined, or all three EPA fuel economy ratings. Both models are expected to have a total driving range of over 500 miles on a tank of fuel.

Picking out a G80 Hybrid or GV80 Hybrid will be a task for Genesis aficionados. Both models purposely look mostly the same as the gas-only options. But distinct details like a redesigned front grille, hybrid-specific wheels and exterior color options will set the more efficient models apart from their gas-only…
items.t: Genesis’ First Hybrids Use a Four-Cylinder. The Torque Matches the Twin-Turbo V6

items.title: 2027 Lamborghini Temerario Spyder: 10,250 RPM With the Top Down
items.summary:
How do you make an already-wicked Italian supercar that revs to 10,000 RPM even better? Easy: take the roof off and give it, uh, an even higher redline. That’s what’s up with the new 2027 Lamborghini Temerario Spyder. It keeps all the savage goodness of the “regular” Temerario, but it raises the RPM limit to 10,250 and loses the top so you can hear it better.

Of course, it doesn’t just lose its top. It merely hides it via a fully retractable hardtop, a first for Lambo in this category. Previously, they’ve been all soft tops. Per the automaker, the roof system utilizes 10 electric actuators to lower and raise the roof quickly and quietly, storing it vertically behind the seats, which is how Lamborghini was able to retain the see-through engine cover in the Spyder.

Lamborghini 

With the top down, the center of gravity drops by 3 mm compared with the closed configuration, while its longitudinal position remains practically identical and the car’s distribution is unaltered. This means the roadster’s dynamics remain just as pristine as the coupe. Per Lambo, a traditional roof setup that stashes away horizontally would’ve raised the center of gravity by approximately 7 mm and shifted it 11 mm towards the rear axle.

The mighty 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 with three axial-flux electric motors remains, along with its 907 horsepower, 118 of which comes from the electric bits. The eight-speed dual-clutch transmission lets it launch from 0-60 mph in 2.8 seconds thanks to its electrified all-wheel drive, and reach a top speed of 213 mph. items.title: This 840-HP Eleanor Mustang Tribute Is a 2026 Underneath Its ’67-Style Skin

Today’s muscle cars are objectively better at going fast than their predecessors. That doesn’t mean they’re better, period. Some folks can’t help but want the drivability of a new V8 speed machine with the look of an old one. Vintage Modern makes vehicles for those people, and this S650 Ford Mustang with a carbon fiber Eleanor lookalike body is the latest. I personally can’t make heads or tails of it.

Everything sounds good on paper, for sure. It’s a brand new Mustang at its core, rocking either a stock 5.0-liter Coyote with 486 horsepower and 418 lb-ft of torque or a tuned version with a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger making 850 hp and 615 lb-ft. I’d be lying if I said that doesn’t sound like a good time. 

And I’m not sure you could do any better with the bodywork, given the parameters. It’s least offensive from the front three-quarter view, when you crouch down low and can’t quite see the rounded roofline. That’s what throws everything off for me. The front looks alright on its own, with all that billet aluminum and the hood that juts out over the front bumper. But the back half isn’t great—at least, not from the side—as the fenders keep going for a mile beyond the rear wheels.

Vintage Modern 

I recognize that I’m not the intended customer for this car. I’d rather have an original 1967 Mustang fastback, one that’s slower and more cumbersome to live with. But I don’t have the money for either of them, so I guess I’ll leave my criticism at that.

items.title: This School Bus Was Repurposed Into the Ultimate Hay Mover—And It Runs Backwards
items.summary:
There are a lot of fantastic tools out there, and I’m convinced some of the best are those you build yourself . If you have a super specific job to do, it’s not a bad idea to forge or fabricate an arsenal of super specialized equipment to get it done. I feel like Dallas Henry would agree, as he has done it time and again—perhaps most notably with a 25-year-old school bus that now operates as a hay loader .

It’s a 2001 International 3800 with a venerable DT466 diesel engine. And while that compression-ignition lump is still under the hood, it isn’t at the front of the loader bus; it’s at the back. That’s because Henry flipped its orientation around so that the ring gear is on the opposite side of the pinion gear, reversing the drive direction. The Allison automatic and auxiliary transmission retain all of their forward gears; the machine simply drives the other way.

“If all tie rods and steering components are right, it works real good,” Henry told me. “Top speed was 36 mph. I recently put a newer rear end that accepts the hub pilot wheels. The gear ratio is a little lower. Haven’t had it on the road to tell. I usually haul it at distances.”

Dallas Henry 

In the field is where this rig really shines. The front-end loader is an Art’s Way 5000 unit built in the late ’60s or early ’70s, originally intended for articulated 4×4 tractors. Henry fabbed it to fit the bus instead, and now he has a machine that will lift as much as 9,000 pounds—more hay than he could realistically skewer with the forks. The hydraulics run off a 22-gallon-per-minute direct-drive gear pump, and the…

items.title: $59K. No Removable Doors. An IPO? Scout’s CEO Just Told Us What’s Real
items.summary:
Two years ago Volkswagen Group revived Scout from the grave, showed off some pretty rad concept cars with some pretty tantalizing specs , and a pretty enticing price. A lot’s changed in the world, and healthy skepticism is only natural when it comes to reviving an iconic automaker.

Now validation units are moving off the assembly line in a 90% completed factory. On the latest episode of The Drivecast , Scout Motors President and CEO Scott Keogh sat down exclusively with The Drive to sort fact from fiction, talk pricing, timing, the competition, and reality.

Keogh’s mission is no easy feat, bringing an American icon back from the graveyard as an EV, making it relevant to generations of people who weren’t even born yet when the last Scout was built in 1980, and developing a complex battery electric platform with a gas engine range extender.

Not to mention, doing all of that under the Volkswagen Group, which got the rights to Scout with its acquisition of heavy-duty truck manufacturer Navistar in 2021. It’s got plenty of other problems right now as sales in China are flatlining and its other EV efforts are struggling, but the reason it’s poured billions into resurrecting Scout is because the Germans know America doesn’t run on Dunkin. It runs on trucks. VW Group doesn’t have any body-on-frame pickups or SUVs for sale in this country, which means it’s missing out on a huge profit center. It sees Scout as critical for getting its finances back on track. Scout revealed its first pickup in SUV concepts in 2024, which somehow was two years ago, and they looked amazing. Too good…

General Motors has reportedly enlisted an executive search firm to identify potential successors to CEO Mary Barra, while also considering some internal candidates. Barra has led GM for 12 years. [ Wall Street Journal ] 

In other Detroit executive news, Ford has announced Vice Chair John Lawler will retire on January 1, following 30 years at the company. The automaker says his role will not be filled. [ Reuters ] 

Google-affiliated Waymo has paused activity of its robotaxis on highways one week after California barred the vehicles from its own highways, based on several instances of them venturing into construction zones. [ Reuters ] 

Jaguar will lean on just 19 dealers across the entire U.K. to sell its new Type 01 EV, down from a network of 83 before this. That’s a 77% reduction, and while those cut dealers will not be delivering new cars, they will remain as Land Rover retailers and/or serve after-sales support for both brands. items.title: We Drove a Manual Chevy Corvette C8, and It’s Exactly What America’s Sports Car Needs
items.summary:
The Chevrolet Corvette C8 was a big pivot for the Bowtie. It wasn’t just the first Corvette with the engine behind the driver; it was also the first to offer a dual-clutch automatic transmission—and only a dual-clutch automatic transmission. After decades of front-engine development, Chevy faced the daunting cost of building a pair of new transaxles (one manual, one automatic) that could mate with a mid-engine car.

Needless to say, developing two gearboxes wasn’t (and still isn’t) in GM’s budget . Now, I wasn’t in the room, and I can’t say exactly how that all played out (and those who were won’t say), but the smart money says that when faced with the choice between either pleasing a vanishingly small group of enthusiasts and winning comparison tests against far more expensive equipment, executives simply chose the latter.

A marketing decision, one might argue, but one that produced a particularly excellent and very capable Corvette. But many of us would still gladly give up a few tenths in the quarter-mile or lap time for the simple enjoyment of operating a manual.

Andrew Collins 

Enter Tremec, the company that built America’s most beloved six-speed gearbox —the transmission employed in GM’s own performance cars, including both Blackwings (RIP CT4) and the also-departed Camaro. And despite rumors to the contrary, its manual C8 development car is quite real . How do I know? Well, I just drove it.

Tremec invited me (along with several potential customers) to sample its whole suite of transmissions at a new (so much so that it’s not on Google yet), private track outside…
items.t: We Drove a Manual Chevy Corvette C8, and It’s Exactly What America’s Sports Car Needs

items.title: Off-Road Guru Develops Budget Portal Axle by Flipping His Jeep’s Rear Diff Upside Down
items.summary:
Portal axles can be a hardcore four-wheeler’s best friend. They instantly elevate a truck, and I’m not just talking about its ride height. I’m talking about its ability to conquer obstacles, whether we’re talking Moab slickrock or Icelandic volcanoes. But there’s one problem: They’re obscenely expensive. That’s what makes this portal axle build by Zeph Gage so interesting. Well, that, and the fact that he’s only installing one on the rear of his Jeep.

Before we go any further, give me a second to explain what portal axles are for anyone unfamiliar. And you know what—actually, allow me to pass the mic to my coworker Andrew Collins , who wrote a stellar story about driving portal-axle Ineos Grenadiers through the Arctic :

“Portal axles are conceptually simple but practically spectacular pieces of engineering that make the vehicle running them much taller than a traditional drivetrain allows. Instead of shafts and other components hanging down from the transmission and transfer case, portal axles put a stack of gears behind each driven wheel.

“That setup lets the axle shafts be tucked up real high, so there’s very little hardware hanging down below the truck’s frame line. Add tall tires (we ran 37-inch BF Goodrich KM3 mud terrains), and you can make enough room to have a picnic under the vehicle while it’s parked.”

My amigo Andrew did a great job assembling some visual assets to help explain how portal axles work. And just look at the difference between a solid-axle Grenadier and one with portals! Andrew Collins

items.t: Off-Road Guru Develops Budget Portal Axle by Flipping His Jeep’s Rear Diff Upside Down
